preceding_messages.text: I adopt the heated-bearing specification, the ten-minute averaging window, and the thirty-percent zero-speed review trigger without modification; they close the bearing-friction hole cleanly. For the bulletin's cross-site summary row, I require that the "neighborhood consensus" wind entry be computed as the component-wise median of the U and V vectors across all sites meeting the sixty-two-percent completeness threshold, never as a median of scalar speed or of compass bearing. The failure this prevents: during a katabatic episode in early April, Sites 1–3 on the valley floor log 3.2 m/s from 270° while Sites 5–6 on the upper slope log 2.1 m/s from 090°, and a naïve median-bearing calculation falls at 180°—the geometric gap—printing a westerly vector that matches no site and implying a phantom valley convergence that, paired with a flat pressure column, reads to a lay reader as a stalled front. I therefore mandate that whenever the inter-site directional spread exceeds ninety degrees, the consensus cell is printed as "SPLIT" with both mode vectors displayed side-by-side and the NOAA comparison cell for that variable left blank for the week rather than populated with the gap value.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the component-wise U/V median, the ninety-degree SPLIT threshold, and the blanked NOAA comparison cell verbatim; they prevent the valley-katabatic phantom-convergence reading without sacrificing the week's otherwise-valid scalar-speed context. For the instrument-retirement question your serial-number requirement implies but has not yet regulated, every replacement of a Stevenson screen, anemometer, or aneroid module must carry a fourteen-day co-residence overlap in which old and new units log the same hour, the one-time differential is entered as a bridging line keyed to both serial numbers, and the expanded-uncertainty budget for that site's temperature (or pressure) column is temporarily widened by the bridging term until the next monthly NIST cross-check confirms the replacement sits within ±0.2 °C. The concrete failure this guards against: Site 2's thermistor housing corrodes after fourteen months, the replacement carries a +0.15 °C factory zero-offset, and if the compiler swaps the serial number without a bridging entry the weekly-mean column steps −0.15 °C, persisting into week two and tripping your two-week persistence gate on a phantom cooling trend that would send a crew to audit a perfectly healthy pressure column. I therefore mandate that no bridging line older than thirty days may be retired from the audit trail, and that any week during which a site operates without its paired instrument logged under the old serial number prints a bold "BRIDGE PENDING" annotation in the bulletin header so a reader never mistakes a one-week instrumental artifact for a neighbourhood-scale shift.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the fourteen-day overlap, the bridging-line rule, and the bold "BRIDGE PENDING" header annotation verbatim; they make the replacement window auditable without reopening the two-week persistence gate. For the reporting question your audit-trail requirement implies but has not yet regulated, every weekly bulletin will carry a SHA-256 hash of the compiled dataset, and a permanent public-appendix section—accessible to any resident by request—where horizon-sketch scans, elevation-survey records, bridging lines, and errata are filed in serial-number order alongside the bound logbook. The concrete failure this guards against: a well-meaning volunteer "corrects" a transcription slip (18.4 → 18.5 °C) directly in the compiled file without entering an erratum line, so the archived logbook and eleven successive printed bulletins diverge by 0.1 °C, and when a resident in year two pulls the bound logbook to verify a cooling trend the quiet discrepancy reads as fabrication and strips the project of its public-credibility anchor. I therefore mandate that any post-compilation edit requires a two-initials erratum entry in the bound logbook and a superseding bulletin issued within five working days, printed with the prior hash struck through and the revised hash alongside, so the audit trail and the bulletin can never silently desynchronize.
